summary: SSE reconnect after auth probe duplicates interleaved choice fragments, causing partial duplicated tokens
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated SSE sessions where, after a short auth probe from an upstream edge (HTTP 401 probe followed by immediate re-auth), the resumed stream contains duplicated and interleaved final-choice fragments. Impact: ByteScale production customers see duplicated trailing tokens and broken JSON choice boundaries in chat completions for ~20% of reconnect events, causing client parse failures and user-facing content duplication. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for ByteScale. Observed since 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC correlating with a change in edge idle-probe behavior. Expected behavior: On reconnect/resume the stream should continue from the last acknowledged offset exactly once; no duplicated token fragments or interleaving. Temporary workaround: Advise the customer to enable client-side idempotency by ignoring repeated tokens between resume events and to disable edge probe if possible.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open SSE session against /v1/chat/stream with token=valid. 2) Simulate an upstream auth probe (short-lived 401 then immediate re-auth and reconnect from the same client id). 3) Let the client resume using last-offset resume token. 4) Observe final chunks: duplicated fragment sequences and interleaving when proxy buffers are replayed. Repeatability: 7/10 on our repro harness using NGINX with keepalive_probe enabled.
observed_behavior:
- Final 'choice' object is emitted twice with overlapping token sequences.
- JSON delimiter boundaries split (partial 'content' fields appear duplicated).
- Client parser throws 'Unexpected token' or concatenates duplicated trailing sentences.
- Example snippet from client capture: '...and that is the conclusion.
...and that is the conclusion.'
expected_behavior: Single, contiguous final-choice block with consistent JSON boundaries and no duplicated tokens after resume.
investigation_notes: 11:40 UTC: Reproduced locally with NGINX probe enabled; fail rate ~70% when probe interval=5s and probe size<100ms.

Hypothesis A: Upstream edge issues an auth probe, short tear-down causes streaming-proxy to replay buffered data while serving-runtime also resumes from the KV cache -> double-send of overlapping fragments.
Hypothesis B: Resume offset semantics mismatch between serving-runtime and streaming-proxy: proxy replays last buffered bytes (inclusive) while runtime expects exclusive offsets.
Trace correlation: request_id=rt-0a9c logged at proxy and runtime; timing shows resume request reached runtime 5ms after proxy replay started.
Related past ticket: SUP-314159 (multiplexed-session-rotation-truncation) noted similar replay behavior but due to different multipath reorder conditions.
Checked metrics: no GPU OOMs; latency spike ~20ms during replay window; no quota errors.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Support (Avery): Thanks for the report. We're investigating; can you confirm whether you see the duplicated fragments in mobile and web clients?
2026-03-12 11:52 UTC - Customer (J. Morales, ByteScale): Seeing it on web (Chrome) and server-to-server aggregator. Mobile appears less frequent.

2026-03-12 12:05 UTC - Support (Maya): We've reproduced and are prioritizing a fix. As a short-term mitigation please try disabling the edge idle probe for your service; we'll follow up with a more durable fix.
action_plan: 1) Short-term (P0): Add a proxy-side deduplication guard to drop immediate replay of bytes seen within last 100ms for resumed sessions (can be rolled within streaming-proxy as config toggle). 2) Medium-term: Align resume offset semantics between streaming-proxy and serving-runtime (exclusive vs inclusive) and add unit tests. 3) Long-term: Add server-side resume idempotency tokens and audits; update runbook to include edge-probe guidance. 4) Postmortem and customer-facing RCA after fix verification.

- QA to validate against NGINX probe and Cloudflare worker repros.
- Notify ByteScale when hotfix deployed for verification window (30m).

resolution: Workaround deployed: SRE rolled back edge idle-probe config for the affected pool; streaming-proxy hotfix with short dedupe cache was canaried to 5% traffic and verified. Result: duplicate final-choice fragments dropped and client parse errors resolved in canary. Planned full rollout pending 24h stability window. Follow-up: alignment of offset semantics and additional unit tests in runtime PR #3245.
